name: Cataratas Del Iguazú International Airport
before:
The airport for Iguazu Falls, and closer to them than to the town it nominally serves. It sits in forest 6 km south of the falls and 16 km south east of Puerto Iguazu, so a client can be at the waterfalls a short drive after clearing arrivals.

It is the easternmost airport in Argentina served by scheduled flights.

The site runs to some 1,800 hectares, most of it woodland, and it is operated by Aeropuertos Argentina 2000. The airport is also listed as Mayor Carlos Eduardo Krause, so both names turn up on schedules and in supplier systems.
after:
The airport for Iguazú Falls, 16 km south east of Puerto Iguazú, the town it serves. Argentina's national parks service lists taxis, remises (private hire cars), transfer firms and public transport from the airport to the national park.

Aeropuertos Argentina runs it, and it is also listed as Mayor Carlos Eduardo Krause, so either name may turn up in supplier systems.

claims.note: Not to be confused with Foz do Iguaçu (IGU), the Brazilian airport on the other side of the falls.

claims.why: Rests on the 6 km to the falls, which has no second source (below).

claims.claim: in forest, 6 km south of the falls
claims.wasBefore: It sits in forest 6 km south of the falls
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. No saved source gives the airport's distance from the falls or describes its setting: the national parks service gives only the town's distance from the park (18 km), and the park concession's and Visit Iguazú's pages give none. geo.mjs checks distances from towns only, and its '6 km south' flag measured from Puerto Iguazú, which is not what the old text meant.

claims.claim: the easternmost airport in Argentina served by scheduled flights
claims.wasBefore: It is the easternmost airport in Argentina served by scheduled flights.
claims.why: Not confirmed. Wikipedia says so, but OurAirports' list of Argentine airports with scheduled service has one further east, Aeroestación Yabotí at El Soberbio, Misiones (longitude -54.11 against Iguazú's -54.47). Whether that aerodrome really has scheduled flights is unknown, so the sources disagree and the superlative goes.

2. SARI IGR Cataratas Del Iguazú International Airport (Puerto Iguazu, AR-N) longitude -54.4734

claims.claim: some 1,800 hectares, most of it woodland
claims.wasBefore: The site runs to some 1,800 hectares, most of it woodland
claims.why: Wikipedia alone gives 1,804 ha, and nothing says most of it is woodland. The regulator ORSNA's site answered 503 and the Argentine AIP's aerodrome pages could not be listed (the browser got 502).
The operator now calls itself Aeropuertos Argentina (Aeropuertos Argentina S.A.). Corrected above.
